our_interpretation: This is a conditional prediction of a causal sequence, with no deadline.

The ordinary reading requires a broad end to exceptional tech-industry growth, followed by a substantial valuation decline that causes at least 20,000 layoffs and an exceptionally severe, sustained regional downturn.
A slowdown at selected companies or layoffs alone would not establish the antecedent or the complete prediction.
The speaker supplies no growth measure, valuation threshold, regional boundary, duration or historical comparison method. I do not invent numerical thresholds for those terms.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes the end of industry-wide hyper-growth and the subsequent causal sequence: a major valuation correction, tens of thousands of resulting layoffs, and a sustained Silicon Valley contraction exceeding previous regional downturns in severity and duration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the antecedent is established, a completed economic episode would need to decisively rule out the predicted sequence. Continued growth or the absence of a depression by an evaluator-selected date does not falsify this undated forecast.
